paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of six different knowledge editing methods on BioMedLM as a function of co-occurrence number, with "Base" representing the unedited LLM. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10^3, with tick labels at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and ranges linearly from 40 to 65. The plot displays six distinct lines: "Base" is a black line with solid circles; "MEND" is a brown line with diamond markers; "FT" is a blue line with triangle markers; "MEMIT" is a purple line with circle markers; "IKE" is a red line with triangle markers; and "ROME" is a green line with square markers. The "Base" line starts at approximately 40% and rises slightly to about 44% before plateauing. The "ROME" line begins at approximately 51% and increases steadily to about 66%. The "MEND" line starts near 45% and rises to approximately 56%. The "MEMIT" line begins near 45% and rises to about 55%. The "IKE" line starts near 43% and increases to about 50%. The "FT" line begins near 40% and rises to about 48%. All lines show an increasing trend with higher co-occurrence numbers, with "ROME" consistently achieving the highest accuracy and "Base" the lowest.
